newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ivory Coast's Octide to buy Dutch cocoa factory.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast's Octide to buy Dutch cocoa factory.

text.p: Dutch Cocoa & Chocolate Holding BV said on Wednesday it was negotiating the sale of its Dutch Cocoa BV unit to a French unit of Ivory Coast's Group Octide.

Octide, based in the Ivory Coast port of Abidjan, trades in rice, cocoa beans, coffee, coconut and rubber. It also owns plantations and production companies and one of Ivory Coast's largest cocoa shippers.

Dutch Cocoa & Chocolate said the acquisition was was in line with Group Octide's aim to move into the production of cocoa products -- such as cocoa powder, cocoa butter, cocoa liquor and chocolate -- both in Ivory Coast and in Western Europe.
Dutch Cocoa & Chocolate said Dutch Cocoa BV, based in Haarlem, was by far the smallest of the six cocoa factories in Europe, with annual turnover of some 60 million guilders.
It was also the last independent cocoa factory in the Netherlands, the other three having long been subsidiaries of foreign parent companies.

Management had felt it was necessary for Dutch Cocoa BV to link up with a large internationally operating company and to find partners in cocoa-exporting countries to safeguard supplies of high quality cocoa beans.
Dutch Cocoa & Chocolate Holding BV said that in future it planned to concentrate on the production and sale of chocolate products through its subsidiary Rademaker BV.
